page.title: Failed Messages
page.subtitle: MassTransit messages a consumer could not process after exhausting retries land in an _error queue, or in _skipped when no consumer claims them. Send them back to the original queue or discard them, one at a time or in bulk.

toast.actionError: The action failed. Please try again.

drawer.title: Message details
drawer.refreshFailed: Couldn't refresh · showing the last loaded data
drawer.goneOrForbidden: This item was removed or you no longer have access to it · actions are unavailable
drawer.siblings: Same event failed at other consumers
drawer.noSiblings: None found — no other consumer failed with this MessageId
drawer.siblingsNote: Matched by the same MessageId · a consumer not listed here either processed it or hasn't failed
drawer.discardStuckHint: If this has been stuck waiting to send back for an unusually long time, you can discard it.
drawer.orderedCalloutBody: This message failed at {{time}}. A newer message for {{ref}} may have gone through since — sending the old one back could overwrite the newer state. Check the current status first.
drawer.nonTransientCalloutTitle: Not retried automatically — needs a data fix
drawer.nonTransientCalloutBody: {{exceptionType}} is on the retry policy's ignore list. If the data for {{ref}} hasn't been fixed yet, sending it back will fail again immediately.
drawer.skippedCalloutBody: Sending it back now will just be skipped again — this only helps once a consumer for this message type is deployed.
drawer.retryAvailableAtBody: The system waits a full 5 minutes after a failure so a retry doesn't get skipped while the original message is still sitting in the consumer's inbox.
drawer.timelineWaiting: Waiting for {{node}} to send it back on the collector's next round

history.retry: {{actor}} sent it back to the original queue

outboxDrawer.title: Outbox message details
outboxDrawer.noConsumerCalloutBody: Resend sets the row back to Pending and clears the retry count; the {{module}} background service then publishes the event again on its next round, not tied to any node. A consumer protected by inbox de-duplication ignores a repeat.
outboxDrawer.newerSentCalloutTitle: {{count}} newer event(s) for the same correlation already sent
outboxDrawer.newerSentCalloutBody: Resending this one now means the consumer receives it after a newer one. It may overwrite the current state of {{ref}} — check the status first.
outboxDrawer.newerSentUnknownCalloutTitle: Can't verify whether newer events were already sent
outboxDrawer.newerSentUnknownCalloutBody: Sent-event history older than 7 days has been purged, so newer events for the same correlation may already have been sent. Resending {{ref}} now may overwrite the current state — check the status first.
outboxDrawer.deterministicBody: This message failed because of a problem with the payload or the event's type, which will fail again the same way every time it's sent. The code or this row's data needs to be fixed first.
outboxDrawer.typeNowResolvesBody: At the time it failed, the system couldn't find the type yet (likely mid-deploy). It can find it now, so a resend is likely to succeed.
outboxDrawer.payloadWarningTitle: Likely a payload or schema problem
outboxDrawer.payloadWarningBody: A resend may fail again the same way. If a new version with a schema fix has just been deployed, it's worth trying — the choice is yours.
outboxDrawer.stuckCalloutBody: A row in this tab has been stuck as Processing for over 2 minutes. The background service normally resets it back to Pending on its own once it's been stuck for a full 5 minutes. If it's still stuck past that, that module's background service may not be running. It can't be resent manually here, because there's no way to tell whether it was already published.
outboxDrawer.timelineOccurred: Recorded in the outbox with the module's data

confirm.tooSoonNote: {{count}} item(s) are still within 5 minutes of failing and won't be sent back this round (available to send back from {{time}})
confirm.retryExcludesRequested: {{count}} item(s) are already waiting to be sent back and won't be sent again
confirm.nothingSendable: None of the selected items can be sent back right now
confirm.retryDescription: The messages are sent back to the queue of the consumer that failed — not re-published, so other consumers won't receive them again. If it fails again, it will reappear as a new row here.
confirm.discardDescription: These messages will no longer be processed, but stay visible under the Discarded tab for the retention period.
confirm.resendDescription: Sets the rows back to Pending and clears the retry count. Each module's background service will publish them on its next round.
confirm.orderedWarningTitle: {{count}} item(s) are on an ordered queue
confirm.orderedWarningBody: may already have a newer message processed. The old state could overwrite the current one.
confirm.nonTransientWarningTitle: {{count}} item(s) need a data fix first
confirm.nonTransientWarningBody: If the data for {{refs}} hasn't been fixed yet, these will fail again immediately.
confirm.skippedWarningBody: They will keep being skipped until a consumer for this message type is deployed.
confirm.newerSentWarning: {{count}} item(s) have a newer event already sent
confirm.newerSentWarningBody: {{refs}} · the consumer will receive the old one after the newer one — check the status first
confirm.newerSentUnknownWarning: {{count}} item(s) can't be checked for newer events
confirm.newerSentUnknownWarningBody: {{refs}} · newer events may already have been sent, but history older than 7 days has been purged so this can't be verified — check the status first
confirm.payloadWarning: {{count}} item(s) likely have a payload/schema problem and may fail again
